rationale: Matthew's own words introduce this as a direct citation, "Then what was spoken through the prophet Jeremiah was fulfilled" (40.2.17), and the quotation at 40.2.18 matches Jeremiah 31:15 almost word for word, differing only in the order of two nouns: Matthew's BSB wording reads "weeping and great mourning," while Jeremiah's own BSB wording at 24.31.15 reads "mourning and great weeping." The label rests on that formula and the near-verbatim match. Jeremiah's own next two verses, included in this range, turn from this weeping to a stated hope that the children will return (24.31.16-17); secondary sources report that Matthew's first readers would likely have heard that reversal in the background of the citation, a reading this connection flags without developing further -- see this lesson's Sources and Limits.
